newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr drifts higher vs yen in Tokyo after trade data.
newsitem.headline: Dlr drifts higher vs yen in Tokyo after trade data.

text.p: 0002 GMT-- *Dollar edged up against yen after Japan's customs-cleared trade surplus came out at lower end of market expectations. Interbank dealers and Japanese investors seen behind dollar purchases.
*Surplus jumped 69.7 percent in July from a year earlier to 849.08 billion yen, and surplus with United States grew 35.7 percent to 420.55 billion yen.
*Forecasts had ranged from a 60 percent to a 114 percent increase in the surplus, or a surplus of 799 billion yen to 1.07 trillion yen.
*Dealers said no substantial offers detected so far on topside.

*"It is not a level at which exporters are placing offers," a dealer at a long-term credit bank said. He said if dollar's topside remains heavy against mark, that may become factor to limit dollar's advance against yen.

*A trust bank dealer said traders had sold dollars in earlier trade on talk that trade data would show sharp rise in trade surplus. But some Japanese investors were keen to pick up dollars near 117.20-30 yen, having pushed greenback up just before data was released.

*A Ministry of Finance official said Japan's trade surplus is unlikely to continue to grow drastically in medium to longer term and that effect of consumption tax rise can still be seen in cars and clothing.
*Mark also rose in tandem with dollar's ascent against yen. It was traded at around 64.66/73 yen at 0013 GMT, compared with 64.55 yen in late New York on Friday.
*A city bank dealer said mark likely to maintain its firm tone against yen but would be top-heavy near 65 yen, where exporters and Japanese investors would be keen to sell marks.

*In New York on Friday, dollar ended sharply lower, hurt by a sharp drop in U.S stocks and mounting speculation that Germany will raise interest rates. The Dow industrials tumbled 247 points to end at 7,695.

*Market now focusing on moves in Japanese stocks and money market rates. Weak stocks, possibly in wake of Dow's decline on Friday, and low bond yields may keep dollar well-supported against yen on downside, dealers said.
*By 0025 GMT, Tokyo Nikkei was down 245.12 at 19,080.91, while key 182nd 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) yield was around 2.075 percent.

*Dealers said market would be cautious about trading dollar/mark given lingering speculation about higher German interest rates and ahead of Bundesbank's first regular policy council meeting following summer recess later this week.
*The city bank dealer said buying interest on dips, which is expected to emerge just above 1.81 marks, will support greenback.
